**Not ready to publish.** Here is the check.

**Product label**

| Product | Label | Hands-on claims |
|---|---|---|
| Pebblebrook Tea Co. subscription | **Not given** | "I've tried four tea subscriptions this year", "easiest to pause", "the tins are lovely" |

I can't assume the writer owns it or has tried it. Until they confirm Owned or Tried (and say how long), the hands-on claims can't stay. If it's Wishlist, all three are cut and replaced with sourced facts.

**Claims list**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "tried four tea subscriptions this year" | Unverified number and experience. The writer must confirm it is true. |
| "easiest to pause" | **Unsupported.** It is a comparative superlative against three other services. Our allowlist supports only "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time." |
| "the tins are lovely" | Subjective opinion. Fine only if the writer has actually handled the tins. |
| "(Affiliate link)" | Correct wording for our policy, but it sits only at the end. |

**Problems**

1. **No product label.** The draft implies hands-on use without saying whether it is Owned or Tried, or for how long. Ask the writer.
2. **"Easiest to pause" is a superlative.** Replace it with the approved claim, or with the writer's own account of what pausing involved if they've done it. For example: "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time. I paused mine by [describe steps]."
3. **Affiliate disclosure is in the wrong place.** The review rules require it at the top of the post, in plain words, before the first link. "(Affiliate link)" next to the link satisfies our brand policy but not the blog's rules. Add a line at the top such as "This post contains an affiliate link, so I may earn a commission if you buy."
4. **Gifted or paid status is unknown.** If the subscription was gifted or paid for, the post must start with "Gifted" or "Ad". Ask the writer.
5. **Approval.** Sam needs to sign off before anything goes public.

**Suggested rewrite, once the writer confirms they've tried it**

> This post contains an affiliate link, so I may earn a commission if you buy through it.
>
> I've tried [number, confirmed by writer] tea subscriptions this year. I used Pebblebrook's for [how long]. Subscribers can pause or cancel any time, and I [describe what pausing involved]. The tins are lovely. [Add what you like about them.] Find it here (Affiliate link).
